items.title: Statement of cash flows: indirect method
items.scenario: Larkspur Industries prepares its 20X6 statement of cash flows using the indirect method. Comparative balance sheets and supporting information are in the exhibits.
items.task: Using the exhibits, compute each amount. Enter cash outflows and decreases as negative numbers (for example, -5,000). Round to the nearest dollar.

exhibits.title: Comparative balance sheets
body: Common stock and additional paid-in capital

exhibits.title: Additional information
exhibits.body:
1. Net income for 20X6 was $180,000.
2. During 20X6 the company sold equipment that cost $100,000 and had accumulated depreciation of $70,000, for cash proceeds of $20,000. It also bought equipment for cash.
3. Bonds payable were issued at par during the year; no bonds were retired.
4. Common stock was issued for cash. There were no stock dividends or stock splits.
5. Retained earnings changed only because of net income and cash dividends declared and paid.
6. There were no other changes in equipment or accumulated depreciation, and no other noncash transactions.

cells.label: Depreciation expense for 20X6
cells.why: Accumulated depreciation rose by expense and fell by the amount attached to the equipment sold. Expense = ending - beginning + removed on the sale.
steps: Add back the $70,000 removed with the equipment sold: 25,000 + 70,000 = $95,000
hints: Build the accumulated depreciation account: beginning + expense - disposals = ending.
Solve for expense: ending - beginning + accumulated depreciation on the equipment sold.

traps.msg: You used only the change in the account. The sale removed $70,000 of accumulated depreciation, so expense is larger than the net change.

cells.label: Loss on sale of equipment (added back in the operating section)
cells.why: Book value sold = cost - accumulated depreciation = 30,000. Proceeds were 20,000, so the loss is 30,000 - 20,000.
hints: Find the book value of the equipment sold, then compare it with the cash received.
A loss is a noncash deduction in net income; it is added back.

traps.msg: Sign error. A loss is added back to net income in the operating section.

cells.label: Net cash provided by operating activities
cells.why: Start with net income, add back depreciation and the loss, subtract increases in receivables and inventory, and add the increase in payables.
steps: - increase in receivables 30,000, - change in inventory -15,000 (a decrease is added back)
hints: Operating assets that grow use cash; operating liabilities that grow provide cash.
Do not forget the noncash loss.

traps.msg: You left out the loss on the sale. It is a noncash charge and must be added back.
You subtracted the increase in payables. A rise in a current operating liability provides cash.

cells.label: Cash paid to purchase equipment
cells.why: Ending equipment = beginning + purchases - cost of equipment sold, so purchases = ending - beginning + cost sold.
steps: Cash outflow, so the answer is negative.
hints: Equipment (at cost) rolls forward: beginning + purchases - retirements = ending.
The sale removed 100,000 of cost, so purchases exceed the net change.

traps.msg: You used the net change in equipment. The disposal removed $100,000 of cost, so purchases are larger.

cells.label: Net cash used in investing activities
cells.why: Investing = equipment purchases (outflow) + proceeds from the sale (inflow).
hints: Two investing items: the purchase and the sale.
Proceeds are the cash received, not the book value.

traps.msg: You left out the $20,000 of sale proceeds, which is an investing inflow.

cells.label: Cash dividends paid
cells.why: Retained earnings: beginning + net income - dividends = ending, so dividends = beginning + net income - ending.
hints: Roll retained earnings forward.
Only net income and dividends changed retained earnings.

traps.msg: You used the net change in retained earnings. Dividends are the difference between net income and that change.

cells.label: Net cash provided by financing activities
cells.why: Financing = dividends (outflow) + bond proceeds + stock issued.
hints: Add the increases in bonds payable and in common stock/APIC; subtract dividends.
Bonds were issued at par, so proceeds equal the increase.

traps.msg: You left out the stock issuance (60,000), an inflow from financing.

cells.label: Net increase in cash for 20X6
cells.why: Add the three sections. The result must equal the change in the cash line of the balance sheet (695,000 - 520,000).
hints: Operating + investing + financing.
Compare your total with the change in the Cash line of Exhibit 1.

traps.msg: You omitted the investing section.

items.title: Basic and diluted earnings per share
items.scenario: Corvane Corp. is a public company with a calendar fiscal year. The controller is computing 20X6 earnings per share for the annual report. Facts are in the exhibits.
items.task: Compute each amount. Enter share counts as whole shares and per-share amounts to the nearest cent. Assume the treasury stock method for options and the if-converted method for the bonds.

exhibits.title: Income and share activity
exhibits.body:
Net income for 20X6: $2,400,000
Cumulative preferred stock dividends for 20X6 (not declared): $150,000
Common shares outstanding January 1: 1,000,000
April 1: issued 240,000 shares for cash
October 1: repurchased 120,000 shares as treasury stock
November 1: 10% common stock dividend distributed to all shareholders of record

exhibits.title: Potentially dilutive securities
exhibits.body:
Options: 60,000 options outstanding all year, exercise price $24 per share. Average market price of common stock during 20X6: $30. Ignore any adjustment of the option terms for the stock dividend.
Convertible bonds: $2,000,000 face amount, 5% stated rate, issued at par before 20X6 and outstanding all year. The bonds convert into 60,000 common shares (already adjusted for the stock dividend). Income tax rate: 25%.

cells.label: Weighted-average common shares outstanding for basic EPS
cells.why: Weight each change by the fraction of the year outstanding, then restate for the stock dividend as if it happened at the start of the year.
steps: Stock dividend applies to the whole year: x 1.1 = 1,265,000
hints: April 1 issuance is outstanding 9 months; October 1 repurchase reduces shares for 3 months.
A stock dividend is applied retroactively to all shares outstanding before it.

traps.msg: You counted the issuance and repurchase for the whole year. Weight each by months outstanding.
You did not restate for the stock dividend. It is treated as if issued at the beginning of the earliest period presented.

cells.label: Income available to common stockholders
cells.why: Cumulative preferred dividends are deducted whether or not declared.
hints: Which claims come before common stockholders?
Cumulative preferred dividends reduce the numerator even when undeclared.

traps.msg: You did not deduct the cumulative preferred dividend. It reduces income available to common stockholders even though it was not declared.

cells.label: Basic earnings per share
cells.why: Basic EPS = income available to common / weighted-average common shares.
hints: Numerator from the income available cell; denominator from the weighted shares cell.
Round to the nearest cent.

traps.msg: Numerator error: net income was not reduced by the preferred dividend.

cells.label: Incremental shares from the options (treasury stock method)
cells.why: Assumed proceeds (60,000 x $24) repurchase shares at the average price. Incremental shares = options - repurchased shares.
hints: The proceeds are assumed to buy back shares at the average market price.
Only the net additional shares count.

traps.msg: You added all the options. The treasury stock method nets out the shares repurchased with the assumed proceeds.

cells.label: After-tax interest added back for the convertible bonds
cells.why: If-converted method: assume conversion at the start of the year, so the interest that year is not incurred, net of the tax effect.
hints: Remove interest expense on the bonds, but consider the tax you no longer save.
Use the stated rate on face.

traps.msg: You added back interest before tax. Interest expense saved is reduced by the related tax.

cells.label: Diluted earnings per share
cells.why: Add the after-tax interest to the numerator, and the incremental option shares and the conversion shares to the denominator.
hints: Both securities are dilutive here, so both are included.
Numerator and denominator must change together for the bonds.

traps.msg: You added the conversion shares but not the interest saved. Numerator and denominator must move together.

cells.label: The convertible bonds are:
options: Dilutive; included in diluted EPS
Included only if the average market price exceeds the conversion price
Antidilutive; excluded from diluted EPS
Excluded because they were issued before the year
cells.answer: Dilutive; included in diluted EPS
cells.why: Incremental EPS of the bonds = after-tax interest / conversion shares = $1.25, which is below basic EPS of $1.78, so the bonds reduce EPS and are dilutive.
hints: Compare the bonds' incremental EPS with basic EPS.
A security is dilutive only if it lowers EPS.

wrong_msgs.Antidilutive; excluded from diluted EPS: The bonds' incremental EPS is lower than basic EPS, so they are dilutive.
wrong_msgs.Included only if the average market pric: That test is for options and warrants, not the if-converted method.
wrong_msgs.Excluded because they were issued before: Bonds outstanding all year are assumed converted at the start of the year.

items.title: Governmental funds to government-wide reconciliation
items.scenario: The City of Eastbrook prepares governmental fund statements (modified accrual, current financial resources) and government-wide statements (full accrual). The finance director is preparing the two reconciliations.
items.task: Using the exhibits, compute each reconciling amount and total. Enter reductions as negative numbers. Round to the nearest dollar.

exhibits.title: Governmental funds balance sheet and other data at year end
body: Capital assets at cost (not reported in the funds)
Accrued interest on bonds (not due and payable)
Property taxes receivable not collected within the availability period (deferred inflows in the funds)
Net position of internal service funds (reported with governmental activities)

exhibits.title: Governmental funds operating statement and other data for the year
body: Total expenditures (includes capital outlay and principal payments)
Capital outlay capitalized in the government-wide statements
Principal payments on bonds (included in expenditures)
Increase in unavailable property tax revenue (revenue in government-wide statements)
Increase in compensated absences liability (expense in government-wide statements)
Change in net position of internal service funds

cells.label: Capital assets, net, to add in the balance sheet reconciliation
cells.why: Capital assets are not current financial resources, so the funds do not report them. Government-wide reports cost less accumulated depreciation.
hints: Funds report no capital assets; government-wide reports them net.
Net = cost - accumulated depreciation.

traps.msg: You used cost. Government-wide statements report capital assets net of accumulated depreciation.

cells.label: Long-term liabilities not reported in the funds (enter as a negative)
cells.why: Bonds, accrued interest not yet due, and long-term compensated absences are not liabilities of the funds' current resources. All reduce net position.
hints: Which liabilities are not due and payable from current resources?
All three items in the data reduce government-wide net position.

traps.msg: You included only the bonds. Accrued interest and long-term compensated absences also appear only in the government-wide statements.

cells.label: Net position of governmental activities
cells.why: Start with fund balances, add capital assets net and unavailable revenue (recognized as revenue on the accrual basis) and internal service fund net position, and subtract long-term liabilities.
hints: Adjust up for items the funds omit (assets, revenue) and down for long-term liabilities.
Internal service funds are reported with governmental activities.

traps.msg: You left out the unavailable property tax revenue. It is deferred in the funds but recognized as revenue on the accrual basis.

cells.label: Net change in fund balances, governmental funds
cells.why: Revenues less expenditures, plus other financing sources such as bond proceeds.
hints: Bond proceeds are an other financing source in the funds.
Expenditures include capital outlay and principal payments.

traps.msg: You left out the bond proceeds, which are an other financing source in the fund statements.

cells.label: Capital-related adjustment (capital outlay less depreciation)
cells.why: Funds treat capital outlay as an expenditure. Government-wide capitalizes it and reports depreciation expense, so add back outlay and subtract depreciation.
hints: Capital outlay is capitalized on the accrual basis; depreciation is an expense.
Net the two.

traps.msg: You added back capital outlay but did not subtract depreciation expense.

cells.label: Debt-related adjustment (principal payments less proceeds)
cells.why: Proceeds increase fund balance but increase a liability government-wide, so subtract them. Principal payments reduce fund balance but reduce a liability government-wide, so add them back.
hints: Debt proceeds and repayments affect liabilities, not net position, on the accrual basis.
Proceeds out, repayments back in.

traps.msg: You removed the proceeds but did not add back the principal payments.

cells.label: Change in net position, governmental activities
cells.why: Add the adjustments to the change in fund balances: capital, debt, unavailable revenue increase, compensated absences increase (expense), and internal service fund income.
hints: Revenues recognized on the accrual basis add; expenses not in the funds subtract.
Include the internal service fund change.

traps.msg: You did not include the unavailable revenue, compensated absences and internal service fund changes.

cells.label: In the governmental fund statements, principal payments on the bonds are reported as:
options: Other financing uses only when refunded
Expenses reducing net position
A decrease in bonds payable with no effect on fund balance
Expenditures (debt service)
cells.answer: Expenditures (debt service)
cells.why: Governmental funds use the current financial resources measurement focus, so principal payments are debt service expenditures that reduce fund balance. Government-wide statements instead reduce the liability.
hints: Which measurement focus applies to governmental funds?
Outflows of current financial resources are expenditures.

wrong_msgs.Expenses reducing net position: Principal repayment is never an expense; it reduces the liability government-wide.
wrong_msgs.A decrease in bonds payable with no effe: Funds do not report long-term bonds payable; the payment reduces fund balance.
wrong_msgs.Other financing uses only when refunded: Other financing uses relate to transfers and refunding payments to an escrow agent, not regular principal payments.

items.title: Liquidity, activity and coverage ratios
items.scenario: Analyst Mina Okafor is evaluating Westgate Supply Co. from its 20X6 financial statements. All sales are on credit.
items.task: Compute each ratio from the exhibits. Use ending balances for liquidity ratios and average balances (beginning and ending) for turnover and return ratios. Use a 365-day year. Round ratios to two decimals, days to the nearest whole day, and percentages to one decimal.

exhibits.title: Income statement data for 20X6
body: Preferred dividends (the equity data above is common equity only)

cells.label: Current ratio (December 31, 20X6)
cells.why: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities. Current assets = cash + securities + receivables + inventory + prepaids.
hints: Add all current assets listed.
Divide by total current liabilities.

traps.msg: That is the quick ratio. The current ratio includes inventory and prepaid expenses.

cells.label: Quick (acid-test) ratio (December 31, 20X6)
cells.why: Quick assets exclude inventory and prepaid expenses: cash, marketable securities, and receivables.
hints: Which current assets convert to cash quickly?
Exclude inventory and prepaids.

traps.msg: That is the current ratio. Quick assets exclude inventory and prepaids.

cells.label: Accounts receivable turnover
cells.why: Turnover = net credit sales / average net receivables.
hints: Use the average of beginning and ending receivables.

exhibits.title: Transactions
body: The Harbor Arts Foundation (a not-for-profit) receives a $60,000 cash gift. The donor requires that the money be used only for student scholarships. There are no other conditions.

A state agency awards the Foundation a $300,000 grant payable as qualifying program costs are incurred. Costs not spent on the program must be returned to the agency. The Foundation has received $150,000 in advance.
The Foundation's board votes to set aside $250,000 of general funds as a reserve for a future building. The board can reverse the decision at any time.
A donor makes an unconditional written pledge of $40,000 per year for three years with no other stipulation. Nothing has been received yet.
Two CPAs contribute audit work that the Foundation would otherwise buy. The services require specialized skills. Fair value of the work is $18,000.
Volunteers stuff envelopes for the annual mailing. No special skills are needed and the Foundation would not otherwise hire staff for the work.
The salaries of staff who prepare donor solicitation mailings total $85,000 for the year. The Foundation reports expenses by function.

cells.label: Item 1 (gift for scholarships): how is it reported?
options: Refundable advance (liability) until scholarships are awarded
Contribution revenue reported in net assets without donor restrictions
Contribution revenue reported in net assets with donor restrictions
Not recognized until the money is spent
cells.answer: Contribution revenue reported in net assets with donor restrictions
cells.why: An unconditional contribution with a purpose restriction is revenue when received and is reported with donor restrictions until the purpose is met.
hints: Is there a barrier or right of return, or only a purpose restriction?
A purpose restriction with no barrier is an unconditional contribution: revenue now, in net assets with donor restrictions.

wrong_msgs.Contribution revenue reported in net ass: The donor limited the use to scholarships, so the net assets carry a donor restriction.
wrong_msgs.Refundable advance (liability) until sch: A restriction on use is not a condition. Only a barrier plus a right of return makes a contribution conditional.
wrong_msgs.Not recognized until the money is spent: Unconditional contributions are recognized when received, not when spent.

cells.label: Item 2 (government grant with barrier): how is it reported?
options: Refundable advance (liability) until the condition is met
Contribution revenue with donor restrictions
Contribution revenue without donor restrictions
Deferred inflow of resources
cells.answer: Refundable advance (liability) until the condition is met
cells.why: A measurable barrier (incur qualifying costs) plus a right of return makes the grant conditional. Cash received before the barrier is met is a refundable advance; revenue is recognized as the barrier is overcome.
hints: Look for a barrier (qualifying costs must be incurred) and a right of return of unspent funds.

wrong_msgs.Contribution revenue without donor restr: Conditional contributions are not revenue until the barrier is overcome.
wrong_msgs.Contribution revenue with donor restrict: Restrictions apply after recognition. Here the condition is not yet met, so nothing is recognized as revenue.
wrong_msgs.Deferred inflow of resources: Deferred inflows are a governmental accounting element, not the not-for-profit presentation.

cells.label: Item 3 (board designation): how is it reported?
options: Net assets with donor restrictions
Liability for the future building
Reduction of net assets with a charge to expense

items.title: Draft financial statement presentation memo
items.scenario: You are a senior associate reviewing a draft memo that summarizes presentation and disclosure rules for the year-end financial statements of Norfield Holdings, a public manufacturer. The controller asks you to correct any statement that is wrong.
items.task: For each numbered statement, choose the option that makes the statement correct. Choose 'Keep as written' if the statement is already correct.

exhibits.title: Draft memo
exhibits.body:
TO: Financial reporting team    FROM: Controller    RE: Presentation matters (draft)

1. Any component that management classifies as held for sale is reported in discontinued operations.
2. Other comprehensive income may be presented only within the statement of changes in stockholders' equity.
3. Gains and losses that are both unusual and infrequent are reported separately, net of tax, below income from continuing operations as extraordinary items.
4. For each annual and interim period, management evaluates whether conditions raise substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the balance sheet date.
5. An operating segment is a reportable segment if its revenue, including intersegment revenue, is at least 10% of the combined revenue of all operating segments.
6. Accumulated other comprehensive income is presented in the equity section of the balance sheet, separately from retained earnings.

exhibits.title: Assumptions
exhibits.body: Assume the entity is an SEC registrant following U.S. GAAP. Facts about Norfield are not needed beyond what each statement says.

cells.label: Statement 1: discontinued operations
options: Keep as written
Revise: only after the component has been sold
Revise: only if the disposal represents a strategic shift that has, or will have, a major effect on operations and financial results
cells.answer: Revise: only if the disposal represents a strategic shift that has, or will have, a major effect on operations and financial results
cells.why: Held-for-sale classification alone is not enough. A disposal is presented as discontinued operations only if it is a strategic shift with a major effect on operations and financial results.
hints: Is held for sale the only test?
Look for a size or strategy test.

wrong_msgs.Keep as written: Held for sale is necessary but not sufficient. The strategic-shift and major-effect test must also be met.
wrong_msgs.Revise: only after the component has bee: A component qualifies once it meets held-for-sale criteria; it does not need to be sold yet.

cells.label: Statement 2: presentation of other comprehensive income
options: Revise: present it only in the notes
Revise: present it in a single continuous statement or in two consecutive statements of net income and comprehensive income
Keep as written
cells.answer: Revise: present it in a single continuous statement or in two consecutive statements of net income and comprehensive income
cells.why: Comprehensive income must be presented in one continuous statement or in two consecutive statements. The equity statement alone is not an acceptable location.
hints: Where is comprehensive income displayed?
It has to appear in a performance statement.

wrong_msgs.Keep as written: Presenting OCI only in the statement of changes in equity is not permitted.
wrong_msgs.Revise: present it only in the notes: The notes cannot substitute for presentation in a statement.

cells.label: Statement 3: extraordinary items
options: Keep as written
Revise: report the item net of tax within discontinued operations
Revise: the extraordinary item classification no longer exists; report the item within continuing operations and disclose it as unusual or infrequent
cells.answer: Revise: the extraordinary item classification no longer exists; report the item within continuing operations and disclose it as unusual or infrequent
cells.why: The extraordinary items category was eliminated. Unusual or infrequent items are reported as part of income from continuing operations, either on the face of the income statement or in the notes.
hints: Does the extraordinary category still exist?
Where do unusual or infrequent items go now?

wrong_msgs.Keep as written: The separate extraordinary items classification was eliminated.
wrong_msgs.Revise: report the item net of tax withi: Unusual or infrequent items are not discontinued operations.

cells.label: Statement 4: going concern evaluation period
options: Keep as written
Revise: within one year after the date the financial statements are issued (or available to be issued)
Revise: within five years after the balance sheet date
cells.answer: Revise: within one year after the date the financial statements are issued (or available to be issued)
cells.why: Management's evaluation looks forward one year from the date the financial statements are issued or available to be issued, not from the balance sheet date.
hints: From what date does the one-year look-forward start?
It is an issuance-date measure.

wrong_msgs.Keep as written: The look-forward period starts at the issuance (or availability) date.
wrong_msgs.Revise: within five years after the bala: The look-forward period is one year, not five.

cells.label: Statement 5: reportable segment revenue test
options: Revise: 10% of consolidated net income
Keep as written
Revise: 5% of combined revenue
cells.answer: Keep as written

hints: Recall the three 10% tests.
Intersegment revenue counts in the revenue test.

wrong_msgs.Revise: 10% of consolidated net income: The revenue test compares to combined segment revenue. The profit test uses combined profit or loss of segments, not consolidated net income.

cells.label: Statement 6: accumulated other comprehensive income
options: Revise: include it within retained earnings
Revise: present it as a liability until realized
Keep as written
cells.answer: Keep as written

hints: It is an equity component.
It is cumulative, unlike the period's OCI.

wrong_msgs.Revise: include it within retained earni: AOCI is reported separately from retained earnings.
wrong_msgs.Revise: present it as a liability until: Unrealized amounts in AOCI are equity, not liabilities.
